questions.prompt: The caller sends request id 3, then receives four notification lines, then a line with id 3. How does it know which line answers its request?
options: The answer is always the next line after the request
It matches the id: notifications have none, the response carries 3
It counts lines and takes the fifth
It reads the method name of the response
questions.explanation: Responses repeat the request's id. Notifications have a method but no id, so they never get confused with answers.

questions.prompt: A plugin in --stdio mode prints debug text with console.log. What goes wrong?
options: The agent stops responding to notifications
The caller tries to parse the debug line as a JSON-RPC message and fails
The text is sent to the model
questions.explanation: Standard output is the protocol channel. Logs must go to standard error.

questions.prompt: Why does each message sit on its own line?
options: The newline marks where one message ends on a continuous stream
The standard requires one request per second
Lines are faster to send than bytes
questions.explanation: Stdio is a stream of bytes with no built-in message boundaries. One message per line lets the reader split them.
